evidence.text: of Present Illness Alex Rivera is a 82‑year‑old individual with a known history of EGFR exon‑19‑deleted adenocarcinoma of the left lower lobe, originally diagnosed at age 78 (stage IIIA, T2aN2M0). The patient underwent video‑assisted thoracoscopic left lower lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection (R0) followed by four cycles of adjuvant cisplatin/pemetrexed and postoperative mediastinal radiation (50 Gy/25 fx) for N2 disease. Surveillance imaging at age 80 demonstrated no evidence of disease. At age 81, Alex presented with a new productive cough and progressive dyspnea. PET/CT revealed a 2.8 cm hypermetabolic right upper lobe lesion, ipsilateral mediastinal nodes (SUV 6.5), and multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules consistent with metastatic spread. Brain MRI was initially indeterminate; a repeat MRI at age 82 showed no definitive intracranial metastases. The patient required a therapeutic thoracentesis for a symptomatic pleural effusion (hospital stay, 2 days). Pathology of the pleural fluid was negative for malignant cells; tumor marker CEA was mildly elevated at 4.2 ng/mL. Since the last visit, Alex’s cough has persisted (now partially controlled with a low‑dose opioid‑sparing cough suppressant), and dyspnea is mild‑to‑moderate (ECOG performance status remains 1). No new neurologic symptoms, weight loss, or fevers have been reported.
